audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch is described only as 'a gap-close charge that knocks up'. Two decisive properties are absent: it knocks up the FIRST ENEMY CHAMPION it encounters, and Riot's own text says Galio 'will briefly step back' before charging.
audit.why: Because only a champion stops it, the dash travels through Mel's wave untouched — minion cover, her usual defence as a rangedless-dash mage, buys nothing against his engage. And the backward hop is a free half-second of warning: it is the tell to spend Rebuttal or walk, and it is the only pre-emptive read Mel gets on his engage.
audit.corrected: The backward hop is the tell; the dash only stops on a champion, so spacing rather than minion cover is what answers it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E: 'briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters')

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer; breakdown.cooldowns said 'It governs your forward steps' without saying for how long.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 down to 7s, Shield of Durand 18s to 14s, Winds of War 11s to 7s, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140. An 11s engage cooldown against Mel's 11s Solar Snare is a near-symmetrical trade timer — the player needs the numbers to know the window is short, not open-ended.
audit.corrected: Gave Justice Punch 11s->7s, Shield of Durand 18s->14s, Hero's Entrance 180s at rank 1, and Mel's own 38s Rebuttal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range relationship between Winds of War and Mel's own spells is never stated, though 'do NOT walk up to throw a wide poke' depends on it.
audit.why: Winds of War reaches 825. Radiant Volley reaches 950 and Solar Snare 1000. Mel wins the poke war outright by standing still and holding her ground — the instruction not to walk up is right, but the reason makes it actionable.
audit.corrected: His tornado stops at 825; your Q reaches 950 and your snare 1000. Poke from the gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places (spikes[2].text, whys[4], late, wants.foe[2]) say Hero's Entrance knocks Mel up 'mid-channel' or bursts her 'out of your own R channel'.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse carries no channel flag in the kit — the flag vocabulary includes 'channel' and R's flag set is empty, and Riot's text describes an instantaneous strike on every marked target. I could not confirm from disk that Mel's ultimate is interruptible, so I replaced the two strongest claims with Hero's Entrance facts that are verifiable (180s at rank 1, 4000-5500 range) rather than leave an unverified mechanic driving ultimate usage.
audit.corrected: Framed Hero's Entrance by its real cooldown and map-wide range instead of an interrupt that the kit does not support.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says what Galio does with his ultimate at 6 beyond using it on Mel.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance reaches 4000 at rank 1 and 5500 at rank 3 and shields every ally in the landing zone. A Galio who hits 6 in a lane he cannot kill in will spend it elsewhere on the map, which makes Mel's job at 6 pushing and pinging rather than dodging.
audit.corrected: At 6 he leaves: the R is a 4000-range collapse on another lane, so shove and track it.

audit.why: The packet flags three suspect ability names here (wants.foe[1] 'Land Shield of Durand', wants.foe[2] 'Hold Hero's Entrance', whys[1] 'Solar Snare's'). All three are false positives — the detector measured the leading verb or the possessive apostrophe. Every Galio ability name in this entry matches the kit exactly.

edits.before: Your Level 1 and 2 are the whole lane — at Level 1 sit at 550 range and auto him, and at 2 with Q + Solar Snare you get one guaranteed root-punish when he steps up to last-hit. Bait his Q (Winds of War) tornado and pop W (Rebuttal) to eat it and fire it back as your own magic damage; that wall is your best tool here. Do NOT walk up to throw a wide poke — his W (Shield of Durand) charges a taunt that drags you into melee, and once he taunts you he winds up free Q-into-passive damage on a target who can't kite.

notes: The packet's three 'probable wrong ability name' flags for this matchup are all false positives — the detector was measuring the leading verb ('Land Shield of Durand', 'Hold Hero's Entrance') and the possessive ('Solar Snare's'). UNVERIFIED, left flagged rather than asserted: four places claimed Hero's Entrance knocks Mel up 'mid-channel' / out of 'your own R channel'. Golden Eclipse's flag set in the kit is empty and 'channel' is part of the derived-flag vocabulary, so the file gives no support for Mel's ultimate being an interruptible channel — but absence of a text-derived flag is not proof, so this needs a League Wiki check. I rewrote the two lines where I could substitute verified Hero's Entrance facts (180s cooldown, 4000-5500 range) and left the wording in 'late' alone. Full-layer verdict fields (diff/diffRating/carryRating/phases[].side/.rating) are shared boilerplate and rejected by the applier's exactly-once rule, so the full layer still scores this 28.57% lane as FAVOURED with Mel winning every phase.
